_comment: Translator's own uncertainty flags. Anything listed here lands on the 'Priority Review' sheet of the reviewer workbook. Key format: 'ui.key' for short strings, 'page:block' for Learn prose. Remove an entry once a reviewer has confirmed it.

fil.learn.discuss_body: Long rhetorical-question chain. Confirm it still flows when read aloud in a classroom.
fil.app.subtitle: Uses 'tala' (poetic/older word for star, and also 'record') instead of everyday 'bituin', to echo the app name. Confirm it reads as 'star' to students and not only as 'note/record'.
fil.track.step_of: 'Step' rendered as 'hakbang' throughout the UI and essays (Hakbang {n} ng {total}). Taglish 'Step' is also common; confirm 'hakbang' does not feel stiff.
fil.p5_feel.nav: 'How each place feels' rendered as 'Damdamin ng bawat lugar' (noun phrase, not a question like the other page titles). Natural, or prefer 'Ano ang pakiramdam ng bawat lugar'?
fil.p6_aspects.nav: 'praise or fault' as 'pinupuri o inirereklamo'. 'Inirereklamo' means 'complained about' rather than 'faulted'; confirm it is the natural pair.
fil.p8_hotspots.blurb: 'chance' (statistical) rendered as colloquial 'tsamba' here and in p8_hotspots.safe99, leg_hot and the essays. Could read as too slangy for a stats concept; alternative 'nagkataon lang'.
fil.p3_places.eps: DBSCAN 'neighbourhood'/'neighbours' rendered as 'kapitbahayan'/'kapitbahay' (also p3_places.k, kd_y, p8_hotspots.radius, essays). CS students may expect English 'neighbor(s)'; confirm.
fil.p2_textgps.mode_repaired: 'Repair' as 'Ayusin' and repaired points as 'inayos na point'. Confirm this reads as 'corrected location' and not just 'tidied'.
fil.p2_textgps.lesson: 'About {pct}%' rendered with spoken 'Mga {pct}%'. Fine in speech; confirm it does not read as the plural marker 'mga'.
fil.p8_hotspots.all: 'share negative' as 'bahaging negatibo'. Alternative 'porsyentong negatibo' may be clearer.
fil.p9_report.c_worst: 'Most faulted' as single word 'Pinakainirereklamo' (also used in essays). Long; confirm it is readable on a report card.
fil.asp.access: Kept 'Access' in English (as in 'access sa health care'). Alternative 'Pagpunta' or 'Abot'. Same for asp.staff kept as 'Staff'.
fil.p8_hotspots.hot: Kept 'hot'/'cold' (and 'Hot cell', 'Cold cell') in English as Gi* technical terms rather than 'mainit'/'malamig'. Confirm.
fil.p4_apart.min_count: 'Minimum times a term must appear' as 'Ilang beses man lang dapat lumabas ang term'. Confirm it is understood as a slider label.
fil.p3_places:p6: 'Rural comments' rendered as 'komento mula sa probinsya' (everyday sense of rural). Confirm, or use 'komento mula sa liblib na lugar'.
fil.p9_report:p3: 'rule of thumb' rendered as 'Gabay lang ang flag, hindi pormal na test' (meaning, not a calque). Confirm tone.
fil.tour.c1: Tour captions c1–c9 were translated by the orchestrator after the main pass; review all nine together for tone (they are burned into the tour video, so a change means re-recording).
fil.app.wordmark_org: 'learning module' kept in English ('Isang learning module ng AIKasalig'), same in brand.module_line, footer.line and about.blurb. Confirm this beats 'modyul sa pag-aaral' for students.
fil.footer.dev: 'Developed by' rendered as 'Binuo ni {name}'. Natural on a footer credit, or prefer 'Gawa ni {name}'?
fil.about:aikasalig: English project title kept, followed by a Filipino gloss in parentheses; 'health misinformation' given as 'maling impormasyon tungkol sa kalusugan' with the English after it. Confirm the gloss is not too long.
fil.about:glance: Month names localized (Enero/Disyembre) and 'Implementing agency' rendered 'Nagpapatupad na ahensiya'. Keep these, or leave the fact-sheet labels in English?

ceb.gate.start: 'SUGDI' vs 'SUGOD' as a game-style START button. Which reads better?
ceb.app.subtitle: Tagline: 'Bitoon ang matag komento. Tan-awa ang gisulti sa mga tawo, ug kung asa nila kini gisulti.' The predicate goes first ('Bitoon ang...') for rhythm. Does it read as poetic, or would 'Ang matag komento usa ka bitoon' sound more natural?
ceb.nav.q_where: I used Cebuano 'mga tawo' (people) in all the new strings, but the existing home.intro uses the Tagalog spelling 'mga tao'. Pick one and make them match.
ceb.nav.learn: 'How TALA works' became 'Giunsa pagtrabaho sa TALA' (also used for learn.nav, learn.page_title, pill.learn, home.how_link). Alternatives: 'Unsaon paglihok sa TALA', 'Giunsa paglihok sa TALA'. Which sounds most natural?
ceb.nav.hint_ordered: 'sunod-sunod' (in order) vs 'bisan unsang han-ay' (any order). Are these clear as small badges next to the chapter names?
ceb.p5_feel.nav: 'How each place feels' became 'Unsay bati sa matag lugar'. Is 'bati' natural here, or is 'pagbati' better?
ceb.p6_aspects.nav: 'praise or fault' became 'gidayeg o gireklamo'. 'gibasol' (blamed) would be closer to 'fault', but 'gireklamo' fits the complaint theme. Confirm.
ceb.asp.access: I left 'Access' in English. The aspect covers distance, transport, referrals and opening hours. Is there an everyday Bisaya word, such as 'Pag-adto' or 'Pagkab-ot', or should it stay English?
ceb.p8_hotspots.hot: I kept 'hot' and 'cold' (and 'Hot cells' / 'Cold cells') in English as Gi* technical labels. A tooltip then reads 'hot 95%'. Confirm this is OK, rather than 'init'/'bugnaw', which might confuse.
ceb.p2_textgps.mode_agree: The location-source options are 'Ayohon gikan sa text' / 'GPS ra ang saligan' / 'Kadtong mouyon ang duha ra'. The learn essay shortens them to 'Giayo' / 'GPS ra' / 'Kadtong mouyon ra'. Check that the short forms are still recognisable.
ceb.p8_hotspots.blurb: I used 'sulagma' for statistical 'chance' (also in learn:why and p8_hotspots.leg_hot). Is it everyday enough, or does 'swerte' (which I used in safe99 for 'by luck') read better everywhere?
ceb.track.finish: 'Tapuson' for the Finish button. Would 'Human na' read better as a button?
ceb.p9_report.in_hot: This is appended after a percentage: '(42% sa mga komento naa sa hot cells)'. Check that the fragment reads naturally.
ceb.learn:chapters: This says Lugar is 'place' in Filipino 'and in Bisaya too', and Salita is 'pulong sa Bisaya'. Confirm that this aside is welcome and accurate.
ceb.p4_apart:p2: Dense formula paragraph. I kept the math tokens verbatim and translated only the connective text. Check that it reads clearly to CS students.
ceb.p3_places:p6: I rendered 'Rural comments' as 'mga komento gikan sa kabaryohan'. I avoided 'probinsya' because it would be confused with the administrative 'province'. Confirm.
ceb.tour.c1: Tour captions c1–c9 were translated by the orchestrator after the main pass; review all nine together for tone (they are burned into the tour video, so a change means re-recording).
ceb.nav.about: 'About the project' rendered 'Bahin sa proyekto'. Because 'bahin' also means 'part', the essay heading 'Part of a DOST-NICER program' uses 'Kabahin sa...' to avoid a clash. Confirm both read clearly.
ceb.about:tala: Heading 'Where TALA fits' rendered 'Asa mosulod ang TALA' (where TALA comes in). Natural?
ceb.about:aikasalig: 'informed by communities' rendered 'giumol uban sa mga komunidad' (shaped with communities), and health given as 'panglawas'. Confirm the register is everyday, not too deep.

ilo.gate.start: 'RUGIAN' as a START button. Natural imperative, or 'MANGRUGI'?
ilo.boot.core: 'Luklukatan ti TALA core' — is the progressive form right for a loading message?
ilo.boot.linking: 'Pagsisilpoen ti text ken location' — confirm verb spelling and form.
ilo.learn.understand: 'Ammuen ti pamay-an' uses 'know' where English says 'understand'. Is 'Maawatan' better?
ilo.learn.try_heading: 'Padasen a sigagagara' — confirm 'sigagagara' is everyday, not literary.
ilo.learn.routine: 'ginagara a panagbaliw' for 'deliberate change'. Confirm register.
ilo.app.subtitle: Tagline rendered poetically, not literally: 'Tunggal komento, maysa a bituen. Kitaen ti ibagbaga dagiti tattao — ken no sadino ti pangibagbagaanda.' Reuses 'pangibagbagaanda' from the existing home.intro. Confirm it reads naturally; a native speaker may prefer 'Bituen ti tunggal komento.'
ilo.asp.access: 'Pannakadanon' (being able to reach) for the 'Access' aspect. Alternatives: 'Akses' (loanword) or 'Pannakagun-od'. Please confirm which is most natural for health-service access.
ilo.p6_aspects.nav: 'Ania ti maidaydayaw wenno mareklamo' (what is praised or complained about) uses passive forms to avoid a verb + '-da' enclitic. 'Fault' rendered as 'reklamo' (complain), not 'basol' (blame).
ilo.p5_feel.nav: 'Kasano ti rikna ti tunggal lugar' for 'How each place feels'. 'rikna' = feeling; confirm it does not sound too literary.
ilo.nav.learn: 'Kasano nga agandar ti TALA' for 'How TALA works' (also learn.nav, learn.page_title, pill.learn). 'agandar' = to run/operate (machine sense). Alternative: 'No kasano ti panagtrabaho ti TALA'.
ilo.persist.forget: 'Lipatennak iti daytoy a computer' — literal 'forget me'. The How TALA works essay refers to it as **Lipatennak**. Confirm it is not too playful for a settings button.
ilo.p8_hotspots.hot: 'hot' / 'cold' (also p9_report.hot_yes 'Hotspot') kept in English as Gi* technical class labels per the Register rule; 'napudot'/'nalamiis' would read as temperature.
ilo.learn.title: Kept identical ('Learn: {title}'): the panel is called 'Learn' everywhere in the existing catalog (side.show_learn quotes it as a name). Translate as 'Adalen: {title}' if the panel name itself should be localized — then learn:tips must change too.
ilo.p8_hotspots.blurb: 'chance' rendered as 'gasat' (luck) throughout (also leg_hot, safe99, essays p8 and learn:why). Confirm 'gasat' is acceptable for statistical chance in teaching register.
ilo.p1_data.toast_upload: 'Napattapatta laeng dagiti column' for 'Columns were guessed'. 'pattapatta' = guess/estimate; confirm everyday usage.
ilo.p9_report.in_hot: Rendered as a phrase that follows a percentage: '(45% dagiti komento ti adda kadagiti hot cell)'. Grammar depends on the code's '({pct}% {in_hot})' concatenation.
ilo.p4_apart.more_typical: 'ad-adda a gagangay iti' + place name for 'more typical of'. Concatenated in code before the place name.
ilo.learn:what: (Applies to all essays and UI) Following commit c47fedb, pronoun enclitics after verbs/modals are written separately (biruken na, idilig tayo, saan da, sungbatan da, malpas mo). I extended this to -da/-tayo, which c47fedb did not show. Possessives on nouns stay attached (saludsodna, kaarrubana), with a hyphen after English nouns (GPS-na, interval-na, write-up-mo).
ilo.p8_hotspots:p3: 'kanatalgedan a basa' for 'the safest reading', and 'Lehitimo a natakuatan dayta' for 'That is a legitimate finding'. Please check the register.
ilo.p2_textgps:p1: 'swapped' (GPS) rendered as 'nabaliktad' (reversed), read as lat/lon swapped; 'default to a device's last fix' rendered loosely. Please check the meaning.
ilo.tour.c1: Tour captions c1–c9 were translated by the orchestrator after the main pass; review all nine together for tone (they are burned into the tour video, so a change means re-recording).
ilo.learn.about_link: Enclitic attached to an English loan: 'dagiti partnerna'. Is that how it is written, or 'dagiti partner-na' / 'dagiti kadua na'?
ilo.about:tala: Heading 'Where TALA fits' rendered 'Sadino ti ayan ti TALA' (where TALA stands). Does it keep the 'fits into the project' sense?
ilo.about:aikasalig: 'informed by communities' rendered 'nabukel a kadua dagiti komunidad', and health as 'salun-at'. Confirm both read naturally.

hil.gate.prompt: 'lenguahe' vs 'hambal' for language throughout. Which do Ilonggo speakers actually use in an app?
hil.side.language: Same lenguahe/hambal question as gate.prompt — keep consistent.
hil.learn.understand: 'Intiendiha ang pamaagi' uses the Spanish loan. Natural, or should it be 'Hangpa'?
hil.app.subtitle: Tagline rendered as 'Bituon ang kada komento. Tan-awa kon ano ang ginahambal sang mga tawo, kag kon diin.' Predicate-first for rhythm; the second sentence trims 'where they say it' to 'kag kon diin'. Confirm it reads as poetic, not clipped. Fuller option: '... kag kon diin nila ini ginahambal.'
hil.nav.learn: 'Paano nagatrabaho ang TALA' for 'How TALA works' (also learn.nav, learn.page_title, pill.learn, home.how_link). Would 'Paano naga-obra ang TALA' sound more natural to Ilonggo speakers?
hil.p4_apart.nav: 'Ano ang nagapabulag sa isa ka lugar' for 'What sets a place apart'. 'nagapabulag' (separates) vs 'nagapalain' (makes different) — which is clearer? Also used in p4_apart.blurb and learn:chapters.
hil.p5_feel.nav: 'Ano ang balatyagon sang kada lugar' for 'How each place feels'. Is 'balatyagon' everyday enough, or too literary?
hil.p6_aspects.nav: 'Ano ang ginadayaw ukon ginareklamo' for 'What they praise or fault'. 'reklamo' chosen over 'basol' as everyday; confirm. Related: p9_report.c_worst 'Pinakaginareklamo'.
hil.p8_hotspots.nav: 'Diin nagatipon ang mga reklamo' for 'Where complaints cluster' — everyday 'nagatipon' rather than the technical 'cluster', since the page title is a plain question.
hil.p3_places.unit_region: Translated 'Region' as 'Rehiyon' (UI option and essays: learn:why, p3_places:p2/p6) while 'Cluster' stays English. Confirm students will not look for the English word 'Region'.
hil.asp.access: 'Access' kept in English: the aspect covers distance, transport, opening hours and referral, and no single Hiligaynon word ('pag-abot', 'pagkadto') covers all of that. Reviewer may prefer a native label.
hil.p5_feel.m_greyed: 'Abuhon' for greyed out (also p5_feel.legend, p6_aspects.legend, p5_feel:p3 'ginapa-abuhon'). Confirm 'abuhon' is the word Ilonggo speakers use for grey.
hil.p8_hotspots.hot: hot/cold kept in English as Gi* hotspot terminology (also m_hot, m_cold, leg_hot, leg_cold, essay p8_hotspots). Alternative would be 'mainit'/'matugnaw', which may read oddly for a statistic.
hil.p8_hotspots.blurb: 'tsamba' used for statistical 'chance' throughout (blurb, leg_hot, safe99, essays p4/p8). It is colloquial (luck/fluke); confirm it does not sound too slangy for a statistics context.
hil.p2_textgps.km: 'nagauyon' for GPS 'agrees' and 'wala nagauyon' for 'disagrees' across p2_textgps keys and essays. Confirm 'uyon' fits a data agreement rather than a person agreeing.
hil.home.peek: 'Tan-awa sing dali ang data' for 'Peek at the data' — Tagalog 'silip' avoided. Is there a more natural Ilonggo word for a quick look?
hil.learn:dirty: Location-source names rendered as **Gin-ayo**, **GPS lang**, **Nagauyon lang**, while the UI radio options (p2_textgps.mode_*) are longer phrases ('Ayuhon halin sa text (rekomendado)', etc.). The English has the same mismatch; check readers can still map them.
hil.p2_textgps:p6: 'ginapilit ang komento sa centroid' for 'snapping a comment to a place centroid'. Confirm 'pilit' (stick/force) conveys snapping without sounding like coercion.
hil.tour.c1: Tour captions c1–c9 were translated by the orchestrator after the main pass; review all nine together for tone (they are burned into the tour video, so a change means re-recording).
hil.about:aikasalig: 'goal' rendered 'tulumuron' and health as 'ikaayong-lawas'. Are these too formal? Alternatives: 'tuyo', 'panglawas'.
hil.footer.dev: 'Developed by' rendered 'Ginhimo ni {name}'. Natural on a credit line?
hil.about:tala: Heading 'Where TALA fits' rendered 'Diin nagasulod ang TALA' (where TALA comes in). Natural?
hil.about:glance: 'Duration' rendered 'Kalawigon' and 'Implementing agency' 'Ahensya nga nagapatuman'. Confirm, or keep fact-sheet labels in English?
